rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A **parallel plate capacitor** (area A, gap d, charge ±Q) derives its capacitance in three steps: Gauss's law gives the uniform field $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0 = Q/A\varepsilon_0$; the potential difference is $V = Ed = Qd/A\varepsilon_0$; and $C = Q/V$ collapses to $\boxed{C = \varepsilon_0 A/d}$ — multiplied by εᵣ when a dielectric fills the gap (NEB 2023, 2024, 5m each).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - E = σ/ε₀ = Q/Aε₀ - V = Ed = Qd/Aε₀ - C = ε₀A/d; C = εᵣε₀A/d

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Between two plates E = σ/ε₀** — the fields of the two sheets add; a lone sheet gives half that.  ·  **Thinner gap = bigger C** — d sits in the denominator.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: When a conducting slab of thickness t (t < d) is inserted, κ → ∞, so C = ε₀A / (d - t). If t = d, the plates short-circuit.  ·  If multiple dielectric slabs of thicknesses t₁, t₂ with constants κ₁, κ₂ fill the gap, C = ε₀A / (t₁/κ₁ + t₂/κ₂).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: definition + derivation (2023, 2024 — 5m each); numerical 2024 3m.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive C = ε₀A/d from Gauss's Law and V = Ed.  ·  Derive C = ε₀A / [d - t(1 - 1/κ)] for a slab of thickness t.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A 200 pF air capacitor has plates 1 mm apart. Find the area.** — A = Cd/ε₀ = 200×10⁻¹² × 10⁻³/8.85×10⁻¹² ≈ 0.0226 m² ≈ 226 cm².

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Write all four derivation steps; state the dielectric extension for full marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Three-step derivation: E → V → C** — memorise the chain, not just the result.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: C = ε₀A/d; with dielectric C = εᵣε₀A/d.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Electrolytic capacitors reach thousands of μF using an ultra-thin oxide dielectric — d tiny beats A huge.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Building Capacitance from First Principles Two parallel plates, area A, gap d: Gauss's law gives the field, V = Ed gives the voltage, and dividing Q by V delivers C = ε₀A/d. NEB 2023 and 2024 both asked this as a 5-mark derivation — the most repeated derivation in the electricity section.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Definition of capacitance (5m, part 1) **Capacitance** C = Q/V is the charge stored per unit potential difference; SI unit **farad (F)** = coulomb per volt. ### 2.2 Derivation of C = ε₀A/d (5m, part 2) Two parallel plates, area A, separation d, carrying ±Q: 1.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 88/89:** E = σ/ε₀ comes straight from Gauss's law. - **To Topic 93:** the derivation gives meaning to C = Q/V. - **To Topic 97:** inserting a dielectric multiplies C by εᵣ via polarisation.
